title: The incident class remains: models and migrations describe different databases.
reproduction: A migration-built database cannot load users, organizations, plans, creatives or jobs. Beyond signup_metadata there are 24 absent columns and 14 absent tables; every mismatch is enumerated in Appendix 1. Local sign-in returned 500 while health returned 200/connected.
fix: Add reviewed, data-preserving Alembic revisions for every Appendix 1 gap; backfill before NOT NULL, and upgrade existing databases before serving the new ORM.

title: A shared external-auth marker is a working password.
reproduction: Create/sync an external-auth user, then sign in with their email and password EXTERNAL_AUTH_MANAGED. The bcrypt exception falls back to literal comparison. Local test returned 200 and an access token.
fix: Reject unsupported password hash formats (return False). Explicitly disable local-password login for external-only accounts; invalidate affected sessions and audit logins.

title: Saving a foreign creative bypasses the scoped creative GET.
reproduction: As tenant B, POST /api/creatives/{A_creative_id}/save, then GET /api/creatives/saved. Full private text is returned even though direct GET correctly returns 404.
fix: Resolve the creative through ScrapeJob and authorized org IDs before saving; add a two-tenant regression.

title: Playbook compilation publishes other tenants’ data.
reproduction: Compile with another tenant’s job_id; the resulting unauthenticated public URL contains their creative. Omitting job_id also selects global patterns/insights without any guessed ID.
fix: Scope all source selections to the caller’s org; validate job ownership before compiling. Restrict public publication to an explicit authorized action and remove contaminated playbooks.

title: Brand and pattern lists are global.
reproduction: Tenant B calls GET /api/brands/ and /api/patterns/. Local fixture returned tenant A’s secret brand and pattern.
fix: Pass authorized org IDs and join through scrape_jobs on both queries; scope counts as well as rows.

title: Insight/simulation creation accepts foreign creative IDs.
reproduction: Generate an insight for another tenant’s ID; the service reads its private body and writes against that creative. A local failing-provider substitute still returned A’s text to B.
fix: Use the same scoped creative resolver as GET before any model call or charge; scope both mutation paths.
evidence: Insight path reproduced; simulation code trace

title: Concurrent charges lose deductions despite FOR UPDATE.
reproduction: Load an org in session A; session B charges and commits; A’s lock query reuses its stale identity-map object. Two 1-credit charges reduced 27 to 26, not 25. Discovery additionally commits its job before charging, releasing its lock.
fix: Make reservation, conditional atomic balance UPDATE, usage ledger and job insertion one transaction; refresh locked ORM rows with populate_existing. Reject insufficient balances instead of clamping to zero.

title: Refunds can mint credits or be lost permanently.
reproduction: Refund the same job twice: balance rises twice (25→27). Two sweepers can select the same stale job before updating and both refund it. A crash after failed-state commit and before refund loses the refund.
fix: Reference the original debit with a unique reversal key; claim failed jobs using UPDATE … RETURNING and settle state plus reversal in one transaction.
evidence: Repeated refund reproduced; sweeper race traced

title: Provider outages produce charged fabricated analysis.
reproduction: Make the provider raise an error. The base class fabricates 92% confidence, proof and performance claims; the caller treats it as success and bills it. Local result deducted 0.5 credits.
fix: Propagate a typed provider error; bill only validated provider output. If an offline heuristic is offered, label it explicitly and do not bill it as AI analysis.
evidence: Synthetic failing provider + real PostgreSQL ledger

title: Transport retries replay paid mutations.
reproduction: Let a Scout/leadgen job or admin credit mutation commit, then drop its response/return 502. The shared HTTP client retries POST/PATCH as well as GET; endpoints have no request-id ledger, so effects can repeat.
fix: Retry safe reads only until mutations implement tenant-scoped idempotency keys and unique stored responses; reuse one key for every retry.

title: Concurrent media jobs bypass generation quotas.
reproduction: Submit several jobs before the first completes. Admission reads completed counters without reserving a slot; completion increments stale ORM values. A five-image allowance can authorize many paid provider calls.
fix: Atomically reserve image/video slots at enqueue, track in-flight usage, settle once on completion, and release once on failure.

title: Workspace data survives account changes in the same browser.
reproduction: User A searches/saves drafts, signs out, then B signs in. Global localStorage keys and a persistent SearchProvider restore A’s searches, active creative and drafts.
fix: Key persisted data by authenticated user/workspace and clear in-memory plus persisted tenant state on sign-out/identity change.

title: A fresh alembic upgrade fails.
reproduction: Run alembic upgrade head on empty PostgreSQL. Revision 46af201944fd drops creatives.source_type, which prior revisions never created; is_impression_estimate has the same problem.
fix: Make the historical transition handle databases with and without these legacy columns; test empty upgrades and upgrades from deployed revisions.

title: Startup changes schema outside Alembic and continues after schema errors.
reproduction: Boot with a restricted DB role or incompatible legacy schema. create_all/raw ALTER statements run in one transaction; caught PostgreSQL errors abort that transaction, yet startup continues. Render start never runs migrations.
fix: Move all DDL and the active-job unique index to Alembic; run a single migration release step; fail readiness/startup on incompatible schema.

title: Health reports success during DB/schema outages.
reproduction: Use the migration-built schema: /api/health returns 200/status=ok/db=connected while sign-in returns 500. A disconnect also retains HTTP 200; /health is unconditional.
fix: Separate liveness from readiness; readiness must verify DB, expected Alembic head and representative critical schema access, returning 503 on failure.

title: The existing gates cannot catch the reported incident or runtime name errors.
reproduction: CI compiles/imports and asserts source strings; no real PostgreSQL upgrade/check or route flow test. SQLite auth tests create_all, hiding migration drift. Build passed despite F35/F36.
fix: Add PostgreSQL fresh/upgrade fixtures, alembic upgrade head && alembic check (with server-default comparison), auth/tenant/billing/job regression tests and Python/JS undefined-name linting.
evidence: Current static tests and build passed; concrete gaps reproduced

title: Forgot-password sends no email and logs the usable reset token.
reproduction: Request a reset for an existing account: the endpoint reports success, but only logs email and reset URL. The user receives nothing; anyone with access to those logs can redeem the link.
fix: Deliver through the existing email service, keep the neutral public response, and remove raw tokens/URLs from logs. Retire exposed tokens and review log retention.

title: Reset tokens are not atomically single-use; stale links invalidate new links.
reproduction: Redeem one token concurrently in two sessions, or issue token B then submit older token A: both requests can read the same usable hash; a mismatched old token clears B. Same-second requests can mint identical JWTs.
fix: Use a random jti and a conditional UPDATE matching the current hash/expiry; consume once, never erase a different current token.

title: Logout and password resets do not revoke stolen sessions.
reproduction: Copy a bearer token, sign out or reset the password, then call an authenticated route with the old token. Only expiry/banned-state checks limit continued use; there is no session version/revocation.
fix: Use short-lived access tokens plus rotating/revocable refresh sessions or a checked per-user session version; revoke on reset/logout as appropriate.

title: Meta access-token literals are committed.
reproduction: Anyone with repository access can extract the two token-shaped credentials from these scripts. Their current provider validity is unverified.
fix: Revoke/rotate them, remove literals, load secrets from the environment, and scan repository history. Do not merely delete current lines.

title: Scout credentials are stored as plaintext JSON.
reproduction: Save a Hunter key or LinkedIn auth cookie. The router writes raw values into organizations.custom_feature_flags; a DB read/backup exposes them even though API flag responses redact them.
fix: Move these credentials to the encrypted workspace-provider credential store and migrate/rotate existing plaintext values.

title: BYOK credentials and the JWT signing secret are accepted in query strings.
reproduction: Generate a BYOK insight or open health?secret=…. URLs carry the provider key or server signing secret into ordinary access/observability logs.
fix: Send BYOK secrets in an authenticated request body; remove the health query secret and use a separate limited diagnostic credential, never SECRET_KEY.

title: URL guards allow private network fetches.
reproduction: Give leadgen a hostname resolving to a private address, or a public sitemap redirect/child pointing to metadata/loopback. The literal-only check accepts DNS names and child/redirect fetches are unguarded. The shared guard also accepts IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback.
fix: Resolve and validate every A/AAAA result, normalize mapped IPv4, bind the validated destination, revalidate each redirect and browser subrequest; add network egress restrictions.
evidence: Mapped-loopback guard bypass reproduced; fetch paths traced

title: The worker reuses async database connections across destroyed event loops.
reproduction: Call _claim_next_job twice with the configured PostgreSQL pool. The first poll succeeds; the second raises Event loop is closed. Running the pipeline creates yet another loop.
fix: Run one async worker main for the process and await claims/jobs in that loop; dispose the engine during shutdown.

title: Background tasks are not a durable queue; Scout/Maps/leadgen lack dead-job recovery.
reproduction: Terminate the web process during Scout/Maps execution or the worker after claiming a leadgen job. Pending work exists only in process tasks; the reconciler covers discovery/media/monitor runs, not these job tables.
fix: Use a durable queue/DB worker with leases, heartbeat renewal, bounded attempts and atomic claims; reclaim expired Scout/Maps/leadgen work and settle credits once.

title: An enabled flag is treated as a live worker.
reproduction: Set SCRAPLING_WORKER_ENABLED=true and stop the worker. Job creation still charges/enqueues indefinitely despite stale/missing heartbeat.
fix: Gate admission on a recent healthy heartbeat/capacity or expose queued state with a bounded execution SLA and automatic expiry/refund.

title: Leadgen bypasses billing policy and overwrites the user’s spend ceiling.
reproduction: An expired/disabled-plan user with balance can enqueue; direct subtraction skips trial/feature/daily checks and UsageLog. Set credit_budget just above base but below computed cost: the route replaces it with the higher cost and charges it.
fix: Use the shared atomic reservation/ledger, honor plan gates and the requested hard budget, and reject estimates exceeding it.

title: Failed Scout/Maps/leadgen jobs retain their upfront charges.
reproduction: Enqueue then fail parsing, provider setup or Scrapling availability before useful work. Failure handlers only set failed/error fields; no reversal is made.
fix: Track the reserved charge and provider consumption; reverse unused amounts exactly once on failure/cancellation, with explicit billing rules for partial results.

title: Provider failure is reported as a successful empty search and charged.
reproduction: Cause every discovery provider to reject/timeout, or leave them unconfigured. All errors become []; the job succeeds with “No active ads” and retains its initial debit.
fix: Return typed provider outcomes; distinguish verified zero results from unavailable/failed search and refund failed execution.

title: Pause uses a stale object and resume never selects the checkpoint path.
reproduction: Pause during crawling: the repeated select returns the cached instance. Resume writes queued, worker claims running, but run_leadgen_job loads a checkpoint only for paused status. Work restarts instead of resuming.
fix: Refresh control fields on each loop; represent resume intent/checkpoint version separately from queue status and claim it atomically.

title: Default AI provider construction raises NameError.
reproduction: Leave either optional AIHUBMIX_API_KEY/TOKENHARBOR_API_KEY unset; MultiTierAIProvider evaluates os.getenv without importing os. Insight creation returns 500 before provider fallback.
fix: Import os (or use validated settings exclusively); test initialization with every optional key absent.

title: Upgraded users remain subject to expired-trial AI gates.
reproduction: Upgrade a user whose trial_expires_at is in the past. AI routing still rejects them based only on user.trial_expires_at and applies the trial 20-usage limit regardless of paid plan.
fix: Use the current organization plan/entitlements; only apply trial expiry and trial-specific request limits to trial plans.

title: Custom swipe creation always fails.
reproduction: POST /api/creatives/custom: app.models.score does not exist. Removing that import still leaves required job_id/brand_id missing and introduces a fake 10,000-impression metric.
fix: Remove the bad import; model an owned manual reference with valid required relations and unknown metrics instead of invented values.

title: Avatar upload calls a nonexistent storage function.
reproduction: POST a valid multipart file to /api/account/avatar. storage_service has no save_file; local request returned 500.
fix: Use store_media_bytes with validated image MIME/content and persist the returned URL; cap size before buffering.

title: Performance crashes as soon as it has data.
reproduction: Open Performance with one creative: avgDays, survivorRate, fatigued and scaling are undefined; survivors is already a number but .length is read.
fix: Compute the missing metrics and return survivors directly; test empty and nonempty page data.

title: Opening a nonempty notification menu crashes rendering.
reproduction: Load a notification and open the bell: <Clock> is rendered but Clock is never imported or defined.
fix: Import Clock from the existing icon package and render-test a populated menu.

title: Support ticket listing fails once a ticket exists.
reproduction: Create a ticket, then list tickets. hasattr(func, "count") itself raises NameError because func is not imported; an empty account hides the bug.
fix: Import sqlalchemy.func or remove the unused count; fetch reply counts in one aggregate if needed.

title: Every Gemini BYOK image call has an invalid argument.
reproduction: Generate with Gemini BYOK. The service passes seed, but GeminiProvider.generate_image has no seed parameter or **kwargs, so it fails before HTTP.
fix: Align the provider interface; pass only supported options and test each provider through the shared call site.

title: Advertised media provider/mode capabilities are not wired through.
reproduction: The provider catalog promises managed Gemini and first/last-frame modes, but managed resolution chooses AIHubMix/Pollinations; the video call does not forward start/end frames. Pollinations image generation ignores reference images.
fix: Publish capabilities from actual configured adapters; implement/forward frame and reference inputs or disable those options.

title: Canceled media jobs can become completed and consume quota.
reproduction: Cancel while the provider is running. The endpoint only updates status; the background task later unconditionally writes completed and records generation.
fix: Cancel provider work where supported; otherwise conditionally settle only a still-running job and accurately explain cancellation/billing semantics.

title: Paid detailed insight fields disappear after reload.
reproduction: Generate an insight containing emotional_resonance/script_teardown/fatigue_prediction, navigate away and reload. Persistence omits these fields; the UI treats the saved result as incomplete and regenerates.
fix: Add migrated storage for the complete validated response and restore it without charging again; include schema/model version and evidence fields.

title: Intelligence invents output after errors and substitutes unrelated translations.
reproduction: Fail insight generation (including billing errors): client code synthesizes high-confidence analysis. Select a pet-related creative and translate: baked Naturia text/forced conclusions can replace its actual content.
fix: Display the real failure and retry action; remove canned translations/teardowns from production paths and render only returned, labeled evidence.

title: New accounts are given fictional search history.
reproduction: Clear localStorage and sign in: DEFAULT_SEARCH_HISTORY restores sample searches, counts and scores instead of an empty state even in API mode.
fix: Default to empty user-owned history; limit fixtures to an explicit labeled demo build.

title: The UI drops the search job ID when compiling a playbook.
reproduction: Finish discovery then compile. SearchContext stores jobId while the page reads job_id; backend falls back to unrelated/global source selections (F04).
fix: Use one typed jobId contract and require an authorized source job at compilation.

title: A transient session failure can leave the app loading forever.
reproduction: Keep a token, remove cached_user, and return 500 from /auth/me. Initial state is loading; error/null-session branches update state only if the token was cleared, so no terminal state is reached.
fix: Always transition to an explicit session-error/unauthenticated state with retry; never leave initial loading unresolved.

title: Team invitations report delivery but shared workspaces do not work.
reproduction: Invite a member: the code returns “Invitation sent” without sending mail. Accept it manually: authorization/default-org lookup only considers ownership, ignoring OrganizationMember.
fix: Send a real invitation and implement selected-workspace membership/roles throughout reads and billing; provide an acceptance route in the UI.

title: An invitation is not bound to its intended email or consumed atomically.
reproduction: Log in with a different email and redeem a known pending token; any user is inserted. Concurrent accepts can both observe pending and insert membership.
fix: Compare normalized invite email to the authenticated verified identity, consume with a conditional update, and enforce UNIQUE(org_id,user_id).

title: App-only updates are exposed by public APIs.
reproduction: Publish an update with show_on_public=false, then request /api/updates or /api/updates/banner anonymously. Neither query applies the visibility flag.
fix: Apply show_on_public to anonymous routes and create a separate authenticated app-update route.

title: Production media falls back to ephemeral storage on incomplete R2 configuration.
reproduction: Omit one R2 variable and generate media: storage falls back to local disk (with a warning), but the job reports success. Restart/deploy the ephemeral instance and the database URL points to a lost file.
fix: Fail production startup on incomplete R2 configuration; permit disk only in explicit development mode and verify storage before settling job success.

title: Twenty provider attempts disable discovery for every tenant.
reproduction: Accumulate 20 ExternalApiUsage rows in a day, including failures; all orgs hit one hard-coded global cap. Count-then-insert is also racy.
fix: Use configurable provider budgets and atomic reservations, per-tenant fairness, and an explicit unavailable response without a customer charge.

title: The impersonation UI keeps using the administrator token.
reproduction: Sign in normally (both token keys set), then impersonate. The UI writes only helix_auth_token while the HTTP client prefers existing helix_access_token, so requests remain admin despite the success message.
fix: Use the shared token setter, clear cached identity/tenant state, and show an explicit impersonation session/exit action.

title: The admin seeder has a public fallback password.
reproduction: Run the shipped seed script without overriding its optional admin credentials: it creates/updates admin@example.com with password123.
fix: Require explicit credentials and an intentional environment; fail if absent and never overwrite an existing admin password implicitly.

title: Pattern generation has shifted arguments, global data selection and no credit gate.
reproduction: POST /api/patterns/generate: the router passes byok_key into the required job_id parameter and byok_provider into byok_key. With no key it selects global recent creatives; with a key it can use the secret as a job FK and fail persistence. It only logs usage, bypassing the paid feature/credit gate.
fix: Require an owned job ID; use keyword arguments and the shared reservation gate. Never fall back to global creatives when an owned job is empty.

title: Provider outages can create false “ad stopped” alerts.
reproduction: After a real baseline, let provider failures produce two successful-empty runs (F29). Monitor diffing treats the missing inventory as actual ad removals, increments missed_runs and emits stopped events.
fix: Only apply diffs after a complete successful provider snapshot; preserve prior state on provider failure/partial coverage and report degraded monitoring.

title: Configured per-plan image/video limits are ignored.
reproduction: Set daily_image_limit/daily_video_limit on a plan. Admission still uses environment image limits and hard-coded trial video rules; configured limits do not determine access. Paid video admission lacks its own completed/in-flight video cap.
fix: Derive both image and video entitlements from the current plan and custom overrides; enforce them in the atomic reservation from F11.

title: Exported playbooks invent confidence and performance lift.
reproduction: Compile from the dashboard: confidence is hard-coded to .92/.95 and lift is manufactured from avg_score with a minimum 5%, without observed conversion/lift measurements.
fix: Remove invented confidence/lift; show unavailable or a clearly named heuristic with provenance and no causal performance claim.

title: Failed reads/saves are displayed as success, empty data or a waking server.
reproduction: Return 500 fetching leads: hook catches it and enters READY with []. Fail save/unsave: Performance still updates the saved badge. A structured worker_offline/provider 503 is retried then overwritten as server_waking.
fix: Keep separate loading/empty/error states, apply optimistic changes only with rollback, and retain server error codes/messages; only label known cold-start failures as such.

title: Paid plans display “Monthly renewal” without a subscription lifecycle.
reproduction: Assign any non-trial plan, including pay_as_you_go: UI says Monthly renewal. Billing routes only expose summaries/usage; there is no checkout, payment settlement, renewal, invoice or payment-webhook flow in this code.
fix: Show the actual manual/beta billing state. Before accepting payments, implement provider checkout plus verified idempotent settlement, subscription state and reconciliation; do not grant credits from client assertions.

title: Stored granular admin permissions do not restrict access.
reproduction: Set restrictive admin_permissions for an assistant-admin, then call admin list/read endpoints. The dependency checks role only and no route consults the permissions JSON.
fix: Define and enforce server-side named permissions for each admin operation, or remove the unsupported permission controls/contract; retain the strict full-admin gate for destructive operations.

title: The XHR-capture option is accepted and stored but never implemented.
reproduction: Set capture_xhr_pattern for a site whose contact data is loaded only through XHR. The worker forwards it into fetch(), which never uses the parameter; the promised data capture does not happen.
fix: Implement bounded capture/filtering with provenance and SSRF controls, or reject/disable the unsupported option instead of accepting it.

title: Provider-resolution failures leave media jobs pending indefinitely.
reproduction: Use a paid workspace with an undecryptable stored Gemini key. resolve_image_provider raises before the task’s try block; no failed state is written. The reconciler excludes jobs owned by the current boot even after their task dies.
fix: Wrap the entire execution path including credential resolution; persist terminal failure and release reservations in finally/error handling. Recover expired task leases even within the same process.

title: Rate limits are spoofable in the app, instance-local and incomplete.
reproduction: Change X-Forwarded-For on requests reaching the app, alternate instances/restart, or use /api/v1/scout aliases/leadgen paths absent from the rules. Buckets never evict old client keys. Public-edge header sanitization is unverified.
fix: Use shared expiring counters keyed by authenticated user/org and trusted proxy-derived IP; cover all expensive endpoints and aliases and bound key cardinality.

title: JWKS cache never refreshes.
reproduction: Authenticate once to fill the process cache, then rotate the signing key/new kid. That process keeps old keys indefinitely and rejects new sessions until restart.
fix: Cache with a bounded TTL and refresh once on unknown kid; validate the configured issuer/audience and require expected claims for each token type.

title: Profile password changes bypass signup/reset length checks.
reproduction: PATCH /api/account/profile with correct current_password and new_password="x". The endpoint hashes it without a shared minimum-length policy.
fix: Use the same validated password schema in signup, reset and profile change.

title: Issued API keys outlive the public_api entitlement and lose workspace scope.
reproduction: Create a key on an enabled plan, downgrade/disable public_api, then use the active key for authenticated reads. Authentication checks only key activity, returns an org, and the user dependency discards that scope.
fix: Return an authentication principal containing key/org/scopes; recheck entitlement and org state at use, and revoke/disable keys on downgrade.

title: Default-organization creation races.
reproduction: Two initial requests for a user without an org both SELECT none and insert. There is no owner/default-org uniqueness rule; subsequent scalar_one_or_none lookups can raise MultipleResultsFound.
fix: Define a unique default-org invariant and use an upsert/transaction retry. Preserve explicit multiple-workspace ownership separately if intended.

title: Hot tenant/job/filter queries lack supporting indexes.
reproduction: As jobs/leads grow, filters on scrape_jobs(org_id,status,created_at), creatives(job_id/brand_id), leadgen_leads(job_id) and the queued-job ordering scan increasing table ranges. The metadata/index inventory shows the missing coverage.
fix: Add query-driven compound/partial indexes via migrations; use EXPLAIN on representative volumes. Index lower(email) if retaining lower(email) login lookup.

title: Several lists are unbounded; support adds an N+1 count query.
reproduction: Accumulate many tickets/users/orgs. These selects return all rows; after fixing func, ticket listing executes one additional reply count per ticket and does not even return that count.
fix: Paginate these collections with bounded page sizes; aggregate reply counts in one query or remove the unused queries.

title: LLM work holds an organization row lock inside a request.
reproduction: Start a slow provider call for one org, then perform another billed operation in that org. The first request holds the spending lock until the provider returns/charge commits, delaying other core flows and occupying a connection.
fix: Reserve credits and commit promptly, run work as a durable job with an execution deadline, then settle the result once.

title: Fetch/upload paths have unbounded time, recursion or memory use.
reproduction: Use a robots.txt endpoint that never finishes, a self-referencing sitemap index, an arbitrarily large media response, or an oversized multipart body. robots read has no explicit timeout; sitemap recursion has no visited/depth guard; media is fully buffered before limits.
fix: Apply connect/read/total deadlines, visited/depth/page limits, bounded streaming reads/uploads and image decoding validation before storage; bound browser concurrency/memory.

title: Scraped strings can become spreadsheet formulas.
reproduction: Scrape a title/name/value beginning with =, +, -, @ or a control character, export CSV and open in a spreadsheet. csv.writer quoting does not make formula cells inert.
fix: Escape formula-leading cells or generate typed text spreadsheet cells; test malicious scraped values on all export endpoints.

title: Polling overlaps requests and stale failures can cancel a newer job.
reproduction: Delay job-status responses beyond 400ms: setInterval starts more requests while previous requests retry. Start a new search before an old poll rejects: the catch checks mounted but not the captured job ID and stops the current poll.
fix: Use an awaited recursive timeout with one request in flight, AbortController and generation checks on both success/failure; choose timeout from the actual job SLA.

title: Datetime serialization and scheduling lose timezone correctness.
reproduction: Serialize an aware invite timestamp: isoformat()+"Z" yields +00:00Z, which JS can reject. Schedule an update at 10:00+03:00: stripping tzinfo treats it as 10:00 UTC rather than 07:00 UTC.
fix: Emit one ISO8601 timezone representation; normalize with astimezone(UTC) before any deliberate naive storage, preferably keep timestamptz end-to-end.

title: Starting another instance can fail a live long-running job.
reproduction: Keep a job alive for >10 minutes with fresh heartbeat, then boot another API instance. Startup reconciliation uses created_at only, ignoring heartbeat and owner lease, and marks it failed/refunds it.
fix: Use the lease-aware reconciler exclusively and atomic ownership/state transitions; never infer process death from total job age.

title: Unvalidated attribution can carry PII into analytics and logs.
reproduction: Visit with utm_campaign=person@example.com then sign up: it is forwarded verbatim to Plausible. A cross-origin referrer that supplies a full URL is persisted with its query; signup logs metadata alongside email.
fix: Allowlist bounded campaign identifiers, strip URL queries/fragments, store only approved referrer origin/host, and redact registration logs; test PII-shaped values.

title: Term/content-only UTM visits are dropped.
reproduction: Land with only ?utm_term=... or ?utm_content=.... These are read but omitted from the condition that persists attribution.
fix: Include all supported campaign fields in the capture predicate and add a small attribution contract test.

title: Keyboard/focus and label contracts are incomplete.
reproduction: Tab through an open ConfirmDialog: only Escape handling/initial focus exists, no focus containment/restoration. Password reveal is tabIndex=-1. Saved draft labels have no associated control IDs.
fix: Use an accessible dialog primitive with focus trap/restore and inert background; keep reveal keyboard-reachable and connect labels to unique control IDs.

title: Backend/worker deploys resolve unbounded dependency versions.
reproduction: Redeploy the same SHA after a new FastAPI/SQLAlchemy/Scrapling release: >= constraints can select a different runtime; the audit already resolved SQLAlchemy 2.1.1.
fix: Commit tested dependency locks/constraints including browser and worker versions; update them deliberately with migration/job tests.

title: Invalid data-source configuration silently enables mock mode.
reproduction: Build with VITE_DATA_SOURCE blank or misspelled: services choose mock without an error. The committed production env currently selects api, so this is a misconfiguration risk rather than evidence the live site uses mocks.
fix: Fail production builds unless the data source is api; require an explicit separate labeled demo configuration for mocks.

title: Long-lived bearer tokens are readable by every script on the origin.
reproduction: Run JavaScript in the app origin (for example, a compromised injected analytics script): both localStorage token keys are immediately readable and remain useful after logout/reset (F19). No exploitable XSS was established.
fix: Use secure HttpOnly SameSite session cookies with CSRF protection or short-lived memory-held access tokens backed by rotating protected refresh sessions; restrict third-party script execution.

title: Additional default/nullability differences make creation paths inconsistent.
reproduction: The diagnostic intended-head comparison found 34 server-default presence differences and three nullable timestamp columns whose models say NOT NULL. These are listed individually in Appendix 1; ordinary ORM Python defaults mask most default gaps.
fix: Choose one explicit contract for defaults/nullability, backfill NULLs where needed, and align models/migrations. Enable compare_server_default in the schema check.

title: Generated artifacts, large modules and duplicated fallback/billing logic raise drift risk.
reproduction: Tracked dist/index.html references an old build; source and generated assets can diverge. Large files and separate generic-credit/image-quota/fallback implementations already disagree (F09/F11/F55). Appendix 3 lists every >500-line source/text file and TODO/FIXME markers.
fix: Stop tracking dist; consolidate entitlement/ledger and provider-error logic, then split large modules by behavior with regression coverage.
